entries.title: Tag evaluators in bulk, and fix an evaluator's name or email
entries.summary: On **Program → Evaluation → Evaluators**, select every evaluator matching your search, not just one page, and **Edit tags** to add, replace or remove tags in one step. A new **Edit details** action (row menu on the event Evaluators tab, the pencil on an Interest Form plan's Evaluators tab, and **Edit Reviewer** in Awards) fixes an evaluator's name and, until they've taken ownership of the address, their email. If the new email already belongs to someone else, Sessionboard names them and offers **Use … instead** to move the evaluator's rounds, assignments and scores onto that person.

where.path: Program → Evaluation → Evaluators (row ⋯ → Edit details / Edit tags); Awards → program → Reviewers → Edit Reviewer; CRM → Interest Forms → form → Evaluation → Evaluators (pencil)

entries.use_case: A committee of a thousand reviewers can be retagged after a track reorganization in one action instead of page by page. When a reviewer was invited under a typo or under two addresses, the admin corrects it from the evaluator list without losing any scoring history.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks how to retag a large reviewer pool, or reports a reviewer invited under the wrong or a duplicate email.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers running Evaluation Plan 2.0, Awards or Interest Form evaluations with large reviewer pools (AUA 2027 Annual Meeting has 1,062 evaluators).
internal.staff_path: Program → Evaluation → Evaluators; Awards → program → Reviewers; CRM → Interest Forms → form → Evaluation → Evaluators
internal.gotchas: Email is read-only once the person has signed in, saved a review, or belongs to another organization — that address is their sign-in, so the admin adds the other address as a new evaluator instead. On the event Evaluators tab, Use … instead moves the evaluator's work on every Evaluation Plan 2.0 plan in the event (the dialog says "this plan"); in Awards it is the program, on an Interest Form the plan. The move is blocked if both records share a round or an assignment.
internal.talk_track: Select everyone matching a search and retag them in one step, and fix a reviewer's name or email right from the list — if that email is already someone else's, Sessionboard offers to move the reviews onto them so nothing is lost.

entries.title: Print booklets include every subsession and its author fields
entries.summary: Booklets for events with more than 2,000 subsessions dropped the later ones, so large poster sessions printed with children missing. Every subsession now prints, and subsession fields stored on the contact or submission record (such as author blocks) show their latest value.
entries.use_case: A poster program with thousands of abstracts prints complete, with every poster under its session and its authors filled in.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports posters or subsessions missing from an exported booklet, or blank author fields on subsessions.
internal.who_should_get_it: Events with large poster programs (event 5920 has 3,169 subsessions).
internal.gotchas: Regenerate or re-export booklets exported before 2026-10-15 to pick up the missing subsessions.
internal.talk_track: Booklets now print every subsession, however large the program.

entries.title: Event colors on the contacts list stay the same between visits
entries.summary: The **Events** column on the organization contacts list painted each event a new color on every refresh. Each event now keeps the same color.
entries.use_case: Teams scanning the contacts list can recognize an event by its color.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks why event colors on contacts keep changing.
internal.who_should_get_it: Organizations with contacts across several events.
internal.talk_track: Event colors on the contacts list are now consistent.

entries.title: Follow-up form submissions now credit the person who submitted, not who opened the draft
entries.summary: The **Submitted By** column in the follow-up form submissions list, the submission summary PDF, and the record activity feed now show the person who actually clicked submit — not the team member who first opened the draft on that record. Historical submissions are being backfilled to correct existing misattributions.

where.path: Portals → [Portal] → Forms → Submissions list (Submitted By column); submission summary PDF; contact activity feed

entries.use_case: Events where a coordinator or admin opens a follow-up form on behalf of a speaker before the speaker fills it in themselves will now correctly attribute the submission to the speaker — preventing false audit trails and eliminating confusion about who provided the data.

cs_action.note: A backfill script will correct ~4,362 US rows and ~304 EU rows where the wrong user was recorded as submitter. The ME region backfill must be run separately after a dry-run. Until the backfill completes, some historical submissions may still show the draft opener. Reach out to Sessionboard Support if a customer reports a specific misattribution that the backfill did not resolve.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports that a team member appears as the submitter of a follow-up form they did not fill in, or raises a concern about data integrity / suspected account compromise on submission records.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using follow-up (portal) forms where admins or coordinators open drafts on behalf of speakers or contacts before those contacts submit the form themselves.
internal.staff_path: Event → Portals → [Portal] → Forms → Submissions list → Submitted By column; also visible in the submission summary PDF and the contact activity feed.
internal.gotchas: Rows submitted before this deploy have submitted_by_user_id = NULL and fall back to created_by_user_id until the backfill runs. The backfill is a one-off raw SQL operation (~30 s on US prod) and does not touch updated_at. The ME region replica was unreachable during dry-run; confirm counts before running on the ME writer.
internal.talk_track: Previously, if an admin opened a follow-up form draft for a speaker and the speaker later filled it in, the admin's name appeared as the submitter everywhere — in the submissions list, the PDF summary, and the activity feed. That is now fixed: the person who clicks Submit is recorded as the submitter.

draft.docs_gap: The portal forms guide should document that follow-up form submissions track a distinct "submitted by" user separate from who created the draft, and explain how the Submitted By column and submission summary PDF reflect the actual submitter.

entries.title: Gatherings and Webinars: new event kinds with registration, attendee management, email, CRM sync, and AI authoring
entries.summary: Two new event kinds — **Gathering** and **Webinar** — are now available alongside the existing conference format. Each starts as a draft and publishes through a dedicated event page. A five-tab **Overview** shows stage, action items, role panels, and a webinar provider slot (Zoom or Goldcast). **Registrations** supports public sign-up, waitlists with auto-promotion, invite codes, reminders, and check-in links. An **Attendees** module stores registration answers in custom layouts without touching Contact records; answers are available as `{{registrant.answers.*}}` merge tags. All 12 gathering/webinar system emails render through the designed-template path with Cc/Bcc and a configurable **From** address gated on a verified sending domain (**Settings → Sending**). HubSpot marketing-event sync writes registrations and attendance back to the CRM on a nightly schedule. An AI authoring flow ("**Make it with AI**") lets Claude draft event-page blocks and email copy; every proposal requires human acceptance before going live.

enable.path: Ask your Customer Success Manager to enable Gatherings and Webinars; then Programs → Gatherings or Programs → Webinars

where.path: Programs → Gatherings / Webinars; Event → Overview / Registrations / Attendees / Settings → Sending

entries.use_case: Organizations running smaller, focused events — dinners, roadshow stops, chapter meetings, labs, or virtual webinars — can now manage the full registration lifecycle, attendee data, branded emails, and CRM writeback inside Sessionboard without standing up a separate registration tool.

cs_action.note: Gatherings and Webinars are behind org-level enablement; the feature is in beta and starts as a draft until the event page is published. HubSpot CRM sync requires HUBSPOT_APP_CLIENT_ID/SECRET env vars and the CRM add-on. Webinar providers (Zoom, Goldcast) require connector setup in Apps.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer asks about running smaller events, roadshow stops, chapter meetings, virtual webinars, or needs registration and CRM writeback without a separate tool.
internal.who_should_get_it: Organizations running field events, roadshows, chapter programs, or virtual webinars that want registration, attendee data, and HubSpot sync inside Sessionboard.
internal.staff_path: Programs → Gatherings / Webinars; Event → Overview / Registrations / Attendees / Settings → Sending
internal.gotchas: Events start as drafts until the event page is published. The verified sending domain gate means off-domain From addresses are server-rejected — customers must complete domain verification before customizing the sender. AI authoring proposals never go live without human acceptance. Value-types 1.13.0 must be published and bumped before the FALLBACK_* constants in lib/attendees/module-constants.js can be dropped.
internal.talk_track: Gatherings and Webinars let your team run the full registration lifecycle — sign-up page, waitlist, check-in, branded emails, and HubSpot writeback — inside the same platform you use for your main conference, so attendee data and CRM records stay in sync automatically.

draft.docs_gap: No existing guide covers Gatherings or Webinars as event kinds; a new guide should document creating a Gathering or Webinar event, the five-tab Overview, the registration flow (public sign-up, waitlist, invite codes, check-in), the Attendees module and custom layouts, the Sending Identity settings, webinar provider connection (Zoom/Goldcast), HubSpot marketing-event sync, and the AI authoring ("Make it with AI") flow for pages and emails.
draft.why_use_it: Gatherings and Webinars give you a purpose-built event kind for smaller or virtual events where registration, attendee tracking, and follow-up matter as much as the program itself. Use it when you need a public sign-up page, waitlist management, check-in links, and automatic CRM writeback — all connected to the sessions, speakers, and contacts you already manage in Sessionboard. The Attendees module keeps registration answers separate from your Contact records so your CRM stays clean. AI-assisted page and email authoring lets your team produce polished event pages and confirmation emails quickly, with every AI proposal requiring human approval before it goes live.

entries.title: Speaker Prospects crawl status updates live and shows a toast when a crawl finishes or fails
entries.summary: The external event detail page now reflects crawl progress in real time via websockets. While a crawl is running, a **Running** badge appears, the **Run now** button is disabled and reads **Running…**, and the status line shows **Running now…**. When the crawl ends, a toast notification confirms whether it finished successfully or failed. Speaker photos that cannot load now fall back to a placeholder instead of showing a broken image icon.

where.path: Speaker CRM → Prospects → External Event → Run now

entries.use_case: Organizers running a speaker crawl no longer need to refresh the page to know when it finishes — the status updates live and a toast confirms success or failure, so they can act on new prospects immediately.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer mentions they were unsure whether a crawl had finished or had to keep refreshing the Prospects page.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any org with Speaker Prospects (beta) enabled that uses the external event crawl feature.
internal.staff_path: Speaker CRM → Prospects → External Event → Run now
internal.gotchas: A 30-second fallback poll remains active while a crawl is running in case the websocket connection drops.
internal.talk_track: Crawl runs now update in real time — you'll see a Running badge and get a toast the moment it finishes or fails, so you know exactly when new prospects are ready to review.

draft.docs_gap: The Pipeline guide (or a dedicated Prospects guide) should document the external event crawl workflow, including the live status badge, the toast notification on completion or failure, and the photo fallback behaviour.

entries.title: Recon: speaker profiles preserved across re-crawls, Sessionize events supported, and live crawl status in the UI
entries.summary: When **Recon** crawls an external event, speakers now retain their **Title**, **Company**, **Bio**, **Photo**, **LinkedIn**, and **X** profile fields — including across re-crawls where the source omits a field. Events that embed a **Sessionize** agenda (such as Ekoparty) are extracted directly from the embed rather than falling back to the LLM, and JSON-LD ItemList agendas (such as Nerdearla) are also read. The crawl status (**Running** / finished / failed) now updates in real time without polling, pushed to the UI over websockets as soon as the job starts or completes.

where.path: Speaker CRM → Prospects → External Events → Crawl

entries.use_case: Teams sourcing speakers from external conferences can now crawl Sessionize-powered events and see richer speaker profiles — with title, company, bio, headshot, and social links — without losing data when they re-crawl. The live status badge removes the need to manually refresh to know when a crawl has finished.

cs_action.note: Improvements are automatic for all orgs with Speaker Prospects (beta) enabled. No action required.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer mentions that Recon was losing speaker bio or photo data after re-crawls, or that they couldn't crawl Sessionize-based events like Ekoparty.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any org using Speaker Prospects (beta) that crawls external events for speaker sourcing.
internal.gotchas: The 'missing never overwrites stored' rule means a field a source stops publishing will not be cleared on re-crawl — this is intentional for this iteration. Corrected values still overwrite. Profile link validation rejects share buttons and links pointing to another person.
internal.talk_track: Recon now keeps the full speaker profile — title, company, bio, headshot, LinkedIn, X — even when you re-crawl and the source doesn't repeat every field. It also handles Sessionize-embedded agendas natively, and you'll see a live Running badge the moment a crawl kicks off so you're not left guessing.

draft.docs_gap: The Speaker Prospects / Recon guide should document the crawl status websocket behaviour (Running / finished / failed badges), the Sessionize extraction strategy, the profile fields preserved per speaker (title, company, bio, photo, LinkedIn, X), and the re-crawl rule that a missing source value never overwrites a stored one.
draft.why_use_it: Speaker Prospects lets you discover and track potential speakers by crawling external event websites, pulling in session and speaker data so you can build a pipeline without manual research. Use it when you want to identify speakers from conferences in your space, compare their profiles, and move the best candidates into your CRM — all without leaving Sessionboard.
